incidents_during_this_run.detail: First launch attempt (nohup+disown, PID 40691) was believed dead when `ps` showed nothing from the operating agent's own shell context, so a second launch (PID 40938) was started against the same --output dir. Both ran concurrently for over an hour, contending for the same model route and writing interleaved records into the same results.jsonl, until both were found alive via `pgrep` and killed. Root cause: `ps`/process visibility from the operating agent's sandboxed shell does not reliably reflect processes it spawned in earlier tool calls. All contaminated pair-1 records from that window were discarded and the run restarted clean.
incidents_during_this_run.mitigation: Always verify with `pgrep -fl` before assuming a background launch died; do not relaunch on `ps` silence alone.

incidents_during_this_run.incident: repeated background-task kill (3x) on pair 4's harness arm specifically
incidents_during_this_run.detail: Three consecutive launches via the operating agent's own `run_in_background` Bash tool were killed by that sandbox at the same point every time: right after starting pair 4's harness arm (go-flutter/bookmarks-app), roughly 10-13 minutes in. A subsequent purely-idle polling loop launched the same way was also killed at the same ~10-13 minute mark regardless of workload, isolating the mechanism to a fixed-duration limit on that sandbox's tracked background tasks -- not a model/network timeout, and distinct from this file's own harness's already-documented 'background-process kills' open item (which concerns `pi` dying in a normal terminal session, not this agent's own tool sandbox).
incidents_during_this_run.mitigation: Relaunched via `nohup ... & disown` with a short-lived launcher process (the launcher itself exits in seconds; the real work is fully detached from the sandbox's background-task tracking). This process (PID 70787) then ran uninterrupted for the remainder of the battery (~1.5 hours). A `--resume` flag was added to run_screening.py so each interruption cost zero already-valid data -- it skips any (pair, arm) with an existing valid record and continues from there.

runner_changes_this_run: Added --skip-task (repeatable) to omit specific tasks from the schedule while keeping the seeded ordering of the rest reproducible.

Added --resume to continue an interrupted run from its own manifest.json/results.jsonl: reuses the prior seed and skipped tasks, skips any (pair, arm) already recorded valid, and appends new records to the same results.jsonl. summary.json is now computed from the full results.jsonl on disk, not just the current invocation's in-memory records, so a resumed run's summary is correct regardless of how many times it was interrupted.

real_findings.finding: Hit the fixture's 45-minute timeout with zero diff and zero recorded assistant messages -- the agent never got a productive turn in. Not the sandbox kill (this arm ran uninterrupted, via the nohup launch, for the full 45 minutes). A genuine stall or hang under the hardened (thinking-enabled) config on this specific task, not yet root-caused.

Hit the fixture's 30-minute default timeout, but the diff it had already made passes the hidden tests (hidden_test_exit=0). The fix was correct; quality-gate's verification/corrective-follow-up loop simply didn't settle and declare done before the clock ran out. Same failure shape already documented in pi-harness-history.md's pair4-rerun-2026-08-13 entry.
real_findings.status: open, matches an already-known failure mode -- adds a second occurrence

real_findings.finding: extension_errors=1: `git-checkpoint.ts`'s turn_start handler crashed with Pi's documented stale-context error (ctx invalidated by a session reload/compaction/fork landing before the handler's first ctx call). stack-router.ts and quality-gate.ts already guard against this exact error class (see lib/stale-context.ts); git-checkpoint.ts had never been given the same guard. The underlying code change was correct (hidden_test_exit=0) but the run is scored invalid per the harness's own validity contract (zero tolerance for extension errors).
real_findings.status: fixed same-day: git-checkpoint.ts's turn_start handler now wraps its body in the same isStaleContextError guard as the other two extensions. 4 new deterministic tests added (pi/tests/git-checkpoint.test.ts), including one that reproduces this exact crash via a throwing ctx.sessionManager.getLeafEntry(). Full 179-test suite passes. Not re-validated against a fresh live occurrence of the same race (timing-dependent, not reliably reproducible on demand) -- the unit test reproduces the exact failure mechanism and confirms the turn no longer crashes.

aggregate.note: Computed from the final (superseding) record per (pair, arm); pair 3's first harness attempt (invalid, 1800s timeout) is superseded by its retry (valid, 792s) after --resume and excluded from these sums, though both remain in results.jsonl.

harness_invalid_reasons.pair_5_dart_sequential-runner: timeout (1800s, diff present, hidden tests would have passed)

interpretation: Among harness arms that completed within budget, quality held (4/4 passed, matching baseline's 7/7) and runtime overhead roughly quadrupled versus the pre-hardening battery's 100.3% median (thinking-enabled turns cost substantially more wall-clock time per turn, as expected). The real cost of hardening showed up as a reliability regression, not a quality one: 3 of 7 harness arms (43%) failed to complete within their existing timeout budgets, versus 0 of 9 in the pre-hardening full-screening-2026-08-03 battery. The per-task timeout budgets (harness_timeout_minutes in each fixture's meta.json, default 30/45) were sized against the pre-thinking harness and have not been revisited since. One of the three failures (pair 7) was a genuine, now-fixed extension defect unrelated to timing; the other two (pairs 4 and 5) are real open timeout-headroom findings.
